body:
1. Thread in Java

A thread is a lightweight subprocess, the smallest unit of processing. Multithreading allows concurrent execution.

2. JVM (Java Virtual Machine)

Acts as a run-time engine to run Java applications. It loads, verifies, and executes bytecode.

3. Four Pillars of OOPs

The foundation of Java: Inheritance, Polymorphism, Encapsulation, and Abstraction.

4. String vs StringBuilder

String is immutable (constant), while StringBuilder is mutable and efficient for modifications.

5. Interface vs Abstract Class

Interfaces support multiple inheritance. Abstract classes can have constructors and concrete methods.

6. Exception Handling

A mechanism to handle runtime errors using try-catch blocks to maintain flow.

7. JDK vs JRE vs JVM

JDK (Dev Kit) = JRE + Development Tools; JRE (Runtime) = JVM + Libraries.

8. Static Keyword

The static keyword belongs to the class rather than instances of the class.

9. Constructor

A special method used to initialize objects; it has no return type and shares the class name.

10. Final Keyword

Used to restrict the user: final variables cannot be changed, and final classes cannot be inherited.
code:
final int SPEED_LIMIT = 90;
final class Vehicle { } // Cannot be extended

body:
11. Array vs ArrayList

Arrays are fixed in size, whereas ArrayList is a dynamic collection.

12. Method Overloading vs Overriding

Overloading is same name, different parameters. Overriding is subclass providing specific logic.
